schedule.rationale: Cutover went live with one of three rehearsals completed and the 1 December run for 180,000 accounts is now at risk (signals S1, S9). The plan has no agreed recovery date yet, so schedule is At Risk.

scope.rationale: Go was approved with 14 open defects, two high severity (S2). Scope is intact but the defect backlog is unresolved, placing it in Problematic.

quality.rationale: Nine-hour portal outage, three further outages from database connection limits, and 4,200 duplicate debits totalling 612,000 euros (S3, S4, S5). Quality is At Risk.

risk_control.rationale: Rollback is no longer possible because meter reads since Monday exist only in the new platform (S8), and the mitigation plan is not yet agreed. Risk control is At Risk.

stakeholder_confidence.rationale: Call waits average 47 minutes at 14,000 calls a day (S7), and the regulator has asked for an incident report (S9). Confidence is at the Problematic/At Risk boundary; 40 is the lowest Problematic score.

risks.description: Further duplicate debits occur or the manual refund backlog stays open, so customers are wrongly charged again and refunds stay late.
risks.mitigation: Block any second debit for accounts flagged as duplicates, reconcile every debit against the billing ledger each day, and move refunds to a daily target with a named queue owner for each batch.

risks.description: Portal outages recur under peak load because the database connection limit is still not fixed.
risks.mitigation: Apply an interim connection limit increase and connection pooling change, then load test at peak volume in a non-production copy before releasing it to production.

risks.description: The 1 December billing run for 180,000 accounts fails or produces incorrect bills, given the open defects, the unfixed connection limit and no rollback option.
risks.mitigation: Run a full dress rehearsal on a copy of production data, close the two high-severity defects first, and hold a go/no-go gate with defined pass criteria before the run starts.

risks.description: The vendor's hypercare team leaves on 30 November before stabilisation and before the billing run is complete.
risks.mitigation: Negotiate a written extension or a handover plan with the vendor lead now, and set a clear list of tasks the vendor must finish before the team leaves.

risks.description: Meter read data created since Monday is lost or cannot be reconciled, leaving bills unsupported.
risks.mitigation: Take a validated backup of all meter reads held only in the new platform and reconcile them against the source readings the team can still obtain.

risks.description: Customer contact capacity stays overloaded, with long waits driving complaints and abandoned calls.
risks.mitigation: Add temporary call handling capacity, publish a status page and scripted answers for duplicate debits, and offer call-back for queries that do not need an agent.

stabilize.goal: Stop the damage getting worse: no new duplicate debits, no repeat portal outages from known causes, and a controlled refund queue.

actions.description: Block second debits for accounts already flagged as duplicates and reconcile each day's debits against the billing ledger.
actions.success_signal: No new duplicate debit appears in the daily reconciliation for the sprint.

actions.description: Apply the interim database connection limit and pooling change, then run a peak-load test in a non-production copy.
actions.success_signal: Peak-load test passes and no portal outage occurs during the sprint.

actions.description: Rank the manual refund backlog by value and age, and set a daily refund target with a named owner for each batch.
actions.success_signal: A complete refund list exists with status for every affected account, and the daily refund count is reported against target.

actions.description: Add temporary contact centre capacity and publish a status page with scripted answers for the duplicate debit issue.
actions.success_signal: Average call wait is reported daily and falls from the current 47 minutes.

recover.goal: Get the project back on track for the 1 December billing run, with the 14 open defects resolved or accepted and a tested run plan.

actions.description: Fix the two high-severity defects first, then work through the remaining open defects with a risk-ranked list.
actions.success_signal: Both high-severity defects are closed with retest evidence, and the open defect count is lower than 14.

actions.description: Complete a full dress rehearsal of the 1 December billing run on a copy of production data within the planned window.
actions.success_signal: The rehearsal finishes inside the billing window with reconciled totals for all 180,000 accounts.

actions.description: Prepare and submit the incident report to the energy regulator, covering cause, customer impact and remediation.
actions.success_signal: Report is submitted and acknowledged by the regulator within the ten-working-day deadline.

actions.description: Agree in writing the vendor support arrangement for after 30 November, or a documented handover plan.
actions.success_signal: A signed extension or a handover plan approved by the executive sponsor is in place before the sprint ends.

sustain.goal: Keep the platform stable, transfer knowledge to the internal team before the vendor leaves, and stop problems returning.

actions.description: Reconcile all meter reads created since Monday and confirm that each has a validated copy.
actions.success_signal: Reconciliation report shows every meter read since Monday is matched and backed up.

actions.description: Run the internal team through the operating runbook, with the vendor observing, for portal, billing and database tasks.
actions.success_signal: The internal team completes the runbook tasks unaided while the vendor watches.

actions.description: Apply a go/no-go rule that bars any release with open high-severity defects.
actions.success_signal: Every change in the sprint passes the rule and the change log shows no exceptions.

actions.description: Keep surge contact centre staffing until call waits are stable for a full week.
actions.success_signal: Average waits stay stable for a full week before surge staffing is reduced.

stakeholder_updates.executive: The billing migration has caused 4,200 duplicate debits (612,000 euros), repeated portal outages and long call waits. Rollback is no longer possible. Decisions needed: approve the staged 1 December billing approach, confirm the vendor support arrangement beyond 30 November, and name the owner of the regulator's incident report. Each decision needs a deadline set by the sponsor, and the date of the regulator's request still needs to be confirmed.
stakeholder_updates.delivery_team: Over the next two weeks the focus is stability. Billing operations will block second debits and reconcile daily. The database lead will apply the interim connection fix and test it at peak load. Defects will be fixed in priority order, with the two high-severity ones first. Please route any duplicate debit query to the refund queue and do not change production configuration without the release manager's approval.
stakeholder_updates.customer: We are sorry for the duplicate debits and the outages you have experienced. Customers charged twice are being refunded, and we are working through the backlog each day. Our portal problems have a known cause and we are fixing it before the next billing run. Call waits are high, and we are adding capacity. We will tell you when refunds are complete and when your next bill is confirmed.

decision_memo.context: The 1 December billing run covers 180,000 accounts. Rollback to the old system is no longer possible, the vendor leaves on 30 November, and the database connection limit and the open defects are not yet resolved. The decision on how and when to run billing must be made now so the team has time to prepare.

options.title: Run all 180,000 accounts on 1 December as planned
options.trade_offs: Keeps the date and the cash timing, but gives the least margin for error with no fallback, a short rehearsal record and the vendor gone soon after.

options.title: Run billing in staged tranches from 1 December, each released only after it passes reconciliation
options.trade_offs: Limits the damage from any fault to one tranche and gives the team time to fix problems, but takes longer, needs vendor support to continue beyond 30 November and keeps the contact centre busy for longer.

options.title: Postpone the run until the platform has passed a full rehearsal
options.trade_offs: Gives the most time to fix defects and the connection limit, but delays customers' bills and cash, needs a new date agreed with the regulator, and leaves the duplicate debit and refund work running alongside it.

decision_memo.recommendation: Choose staged tranches (option 2), with each tranche released only after a go/no-go gate and reconciliation against meter reads. Make the first tranche conditional on the database fix passing peak-load testing, both high-severity defects closed and a secured vendor arrangement beyond 30 November. If the conditions are not met by the date the sponsor sets, move to postponement (option 3). Staged release contains the risk, while postponement remains the fallback.
